title: Shrimp and Grits Breakfast
subtitle: Creamy stone-ground grits topped with Cajun-spiced shrimp and andouille.
description: Adapted from classic Lowcountry Carolina breakfast tradition for firehall service: slow-stirred stone-ground grits with sharp cheddar, topped with sautéed shrimp, andouille, and a pan sauce bright with lemon and scallions.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Shrimp and Grits Breakfast in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook the grits
steps.instruction: Bring milk and water to a gentle boil in a heavy pot. Whisk in grits, reduce to low, and cook 20–25 minutes stirring often until thick and creamy. Fold in cheddar, butter, salt, and pepper; hold covered on low. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Brown the andouille
steps.instruction: Sauté andouille coins in a large skillet over medium-high until edges crisp and fat renders, about 5 minutes. Transfer to a warm plate, leaving fat in the pan. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear the shrimp
steps.instruction: Pat shrimp dry, toss with Cajun seasoning, and sear in the andouille fat over high heat in a single layer. Cook 2 minutes per side until pink and internal temperature reaches 145°F. Do not overcrowd. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the pan sauce
steps.instruction: Return andouille to the pan with shrimp. Add a splash of water or stock, scrape browned bits, and finish with lemon juice and half the scallions. Taste and adjust salt. Plan about 4 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.instruction: Spoon creamy grits into warm bowls, top with shrimp-andouille mixture, and garnish with remaining scallions and lemon wedges. Serve immediately while grits stay loose. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Start grits first—they need constant stirring and cannot wait for shrimp to finish.
Pat shrimp completely dry before seasoning or they steam instead of sear.
Hold grits in a bain-marie on low with a splash of milk stirred in every 10 minutes.
cleanupNotes: Fill the grits pot with hot water immediately—starch sets like concrete once cooled.
Rinse shrimp shells and prep surfaces with sanitizer before handling other ingredients.
leftovers: Grits tighten when chilled; reheat with milk whisked in over low heat until creamy again.
Chop leftover shrimp into a breakfast taco filling with hot sauce and scrambled eggs.
